units.note: Final [...] marks the excerpt break; the sentence continues at the start of ch. 13 (τῆς | προθέσεως), so no lacuna is being smoothed.

findings.quote: For it was necessary, he said, not for the Lacedaemonians or the Romans to be troubled in this way, but rather for those among their own people who cooperated with the enemy;
findings.problem: δεῖν γὰρ οὐ Λακεδαιμονίους οὐδὲ Ῥωμαίους ἀγωνιᾶν οὕτως ὡς τοὺς ἐξ αὐτῶν συνεργοῦντας τοῖς ἐχθροῖς: the accusatives are the objects of ἀγωνιᾶν (to fear / be anxious about), with οὐ … οὕτως ὡς = 'not so much … as'. The Achaeans should fear not the Lacedaemonians or Romans so much as the traitors among them. The English makes the Lacedaemonians and Romans the ones who are troubled, which inverts the sense.
findings.proposed_fix: For they ought not to fear the Lacedaemonians or the Romans so much as those among their own people who cooperated with the enemy;

findings.problem: The Greek has Φιλεταίρου, i.e. Philetaerus (the Attalid brother of Eumenes II). The English misspells the name.

units.note: The Latin testimonium (Orosius, on the battle under Critolaus and the defeat of Diaeus by Metellus) printed after the Greek has no English rendering. That is apparatus, not a lacuna, so it is flagged here only for Phase 6.

findings.quote: a total of ten thousand men
findings.problem: εἰς μυρίους καὶ δισχιλίους = to the number of twelve thousand (10,000 + 2,000).
findings.proposed_fix: a total of twelve thousand men

findings.problem: ἠλᾶτο κατὰ τῆς χώρας = he wandered about the country, meaning within the Peloponnese he had withdrawn to. The English says he was expelled from it, which inverts the sense.

findings.quote: For though they clearly knew what they had done
findings.problem: σαφῶς γὰρ σφίσι τὰ πεπραγμένα συνειδότες is causal: it is because they were conscious of what they had done that they could not believe they would find mercy. The English 'though' turns the causal participle into a concession, which reverses the logic.
findings.proposed_fix: For since they clearly knew what they had done

findings.quote: even though they were all equally in the wrong
findings.problem: εἰ καὶ πάντων ἅμα διήμαρτον: πάντων is the genitive of the thing missed with διαμαρτάνω ('even though they failed of everything at once / missed the mark entirely'). It is not a subject 'they all'. The English misreads the construction.
findings.proposed_fix: even though they failed utterly in everything

findings.quote: but believed that Philon was speaking because he privately placed his own interest and security above everything else
findings.problem: ἀλλ᾽ αὐτοὺς κατ᾽ ἰδίαν τὸ σφέτερον συμφέρον … τιθεμένους ταῦτα λέγειν: the plural αὐτοὺς … τιθεμένους refers to those urging acceptance (Stratius and his associates, possibly with Philon), and the councillors mean their own private interest. The Greek does not single out Philon. The English names the wrong referent.
findings.proposed_fix: but believed that those urging this were speaking because they privately placed their own interest and security above everything else

units.note: Outside my error classes, so no finding is made: 'who had just gained influence' renders ἄρτι τῆς καθόδου τετευχώς, which means 'having just obtained his return from exile'. Also 'think only of the immediate situation' loosely renders πρὸς τοῦτον τὸν σκοπὸν ἐβουλεύσαντο περὶ τῶν ἐνεστώτων ('deliberated on the present situation with this aim').
